title: Prompt-injected document/tool result causes an unauthorized tool action
bad_event: A sensitive action whose authorization-relevant arguments are derived, through label-propagating steps, from tool results executes without a fresh user confirmation of exactly its tool and values. 'Untrusted' is defined by derivation from tool results; laundering is excluded STRUCTURALLY in the planner-isolation design (SC23Isolation: planner state holds only trusted values or handles; noninterference; w1_impossible), leaving as premises an authenticated user channel and no side channel from quarantined processing (REVIEW-PACKET finding 4). Read "by X" as "by an operation carrying X's authenticated identity" (credential separation is a premise, not a theorem).
adversary: Model: any trace of tool results (tainted), derivations with arbitrary content, confirmations by any caller and actions with any arguments.
refutation: An executed sensitive action with tainted arguments and no exact confirmation despite full checks (witnesses: non-propagating summarizer, paraphrase confirmation, confirmation reuse).
scope: Lean model only; no runtime harness. Not: wisdom of confirmations, correctness of untainted values, planner isolation.

assumptions.text: Every operation carrying a trusted role's identity (approver, reviewer, admin, auditor, verifier, user) is that principal's own act: agents cannot obtain or forge trusted identities. Not modelled: the Lean models read caller identity as authenticated (REVIEW-PACKET-2026-10-09 finding 1).
Labels reflect true provenance: the planner never reads untrusted data except through labelled values. This premise carries the anti-laundering burden.
The confirmation UI shows exact values and only users can confirm.
Confirmation burden on honest tasks is acceptable.
